themes.label: Building Commemoration
themes.rationale: The term 'ktistes' (founder/builder) explicitly identifies the individual as the person responsible for the construction or foundation of the building, which is a standard building commemoration formula.

themes.label: Acclamations and Slogans
themes.rationale: The word 'eutychos' (happily/fortunately) is a common acclamatory formula used in Late Antiquity to wish good fortune upon a person or a project.

themes.label: Honorific Inscriptions
themes.rationale: Designating someone as 'the founder' (ktistes) serves as an honorific title, acknowledging their contribution to the community or the state.

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The inscription is highly broken, with significant portions of the text missing and requiring reconstruction.

rationale: This Late Antique inscription from the imperial revenue office in Caesarea Maritima commemorates a founder, likely named Eugenius (reconstructed from 'Eug-'). It utilizes the standard acclamatory formula 'eutychos' to celebrate the individual's role as 'ktistes' (founder/builder). The context of an imperial office suggests the individual may have been a high-ranking official involved in the building's renovation or construction during the 5th or 6th century AD.
